resources.string: Warden only switches off Developer options, USB and wireless debugging, and accessibility apps while a watched app is open, and always puts back exactly what was on.
Lets Warden see which app is in front. Nothing leaves the phone.
Switch greyed out, or a \"Restricted setting\" message? Open app settings, tap the three-dot menu, choose Allow restricted settings, then try again.
A one-time grant through adb. It survives reboots and updates.
Connect the phone to a computer with adb (USB or Wireless debugging).
Run this. This screen updates by itself.
Developer options are off. Tap Build number 7 times in About phone.
Xiaomi, Redmi, Poco: if it fails, turn on USB debugging (Security settings) in Developer options and run it again.
Oppo, Realme, OnePlus: if it fails, turn on Disable permission monitoring in Developer options and run it again.
Rather skip the computer? Use Shizuku
The simpler way: Shizuku does the same grant right on the phone, using Wireless debugging. You can remove it afterward.
Turn on Wireless debugging in Developer options. Wi-Fi must be on.
In Shizuku, tap Pairing and enter the code from Wireless debugging > Pair device with pairing code. Then tap Start.
Return to Warden, tap Grant with Shizuku, then Allow.
Allow Warden in Shizuku, then try again.
Shizuku couldn\'t grant it. Use the computer steps above.
Stops the system from putting Warden to sleep while it is watching.
On Samsung, also set Battery to Unrestricted and keep Warden out of Sleeping apps.
On Xiaomi, Redmi and Poco, also open app settings: turn on Autostart and set Battery saver to No restrictions.
On Oppo, Realme and OnePlus, also open app settings, tap Battery usage and turn on Allow background activity and Allow auto launch.
On Vivo and iQOO, also open app settings, tap Battery and allow high background power consumption. Turn on Autostart if your phone shows it.
Battery usage for Warden is set to Restricted, which stops it in the background. Open app settings, tap Battery and choose Unrestricted.

Android pauses apps you haven\'t opened in months and removes their permissions. Warden works in the background, so turn this off for it: \"Manage app if unused\" on Samsung, \"Pause app activity if unused\" on other phones.
Samsung: Settings > Battery > Background usage limits > Never sleeping apps, then add Warden. Also check it isn\'t listed under Sleeping or Deep sleeping apps.
Samsung: open Recents, tap Warden\'s icon and choose Keep open, so Close all won\'t stop it.
Open Recents, long-press Warden (or tap its menu) and choose Lock, so Clear all won\'t stop it.
Don\'t force stop Warden. If you do, open it once and it restarts the monitor.
To hide the status notification, tap Hide on it and turn off Monitor. Warden keeps working. Keep Alerts on - that\'s how it tells you a setting didn\'t switch.
Reinstalling Warden removes the grant. Do that step again afterward.
Shows what Warden is doing and alerts you if a setting can\'t be switched off or back on.
